name: Comendador Joan Escrivá
bio: Joan Escrivá (fl. 1470-1497), called the Comendador, was a Valencian courtier and poet who wrote in Castilian. His verse was gathered in the Cancionero general (Valencia, 1511).

He is remembered above all for one short canción, 'Ven muerte tan escondida', a plea that death come so quietly that the joy of its coming may not call the dying back to life. The poem was glossed and imitated by Spanish poets for two centuries.

poems.title: Canción: Ven muerte tan escondida
poems.author: Comendador Joan Escrivá
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Spanish Verse (1913)
poems.note: Spanish original, from the Cancionero general (1511); the English translation by John Bowring follows as the next poem.
poems.text:
Ven muerte tan escondida
que no te sienta comigo,
porqu' el gozo de contigo
no me torne a dar la vida.

Ven como rayo que hiere,
que hasta que ha herido
no se siente su ruydo,
por mejor herir do quiere:
assi sea tu venida,
si no, desde aqui me obligo
qu' el gozo que aure contigo
me dara de nuevo vida.

poems.title: Welcome, Death!
poems.author: Comendador Joan Escrivá
poems.collection: Ancient Poetry and Romances of Spain (1824)
poems.note: Translation of the canción 'Ven muerte tan escondida' (the Spanish original is the preceding poem).
poems.text:
Come, gentle death! come silently,
And sound no knell, no warning give,
Lest the sweet bliss of welcoming thee
Should rouse my wearied soul to live.

Come like the rapid lightning's ray,
That wounds, but while it wounds is still;
It passes, voiceless, on its way,
And flings its mortal barb at will.
Thus soft, thus calm, thy coming be,
Else, death! this warning now I give,
That the sweet bliss of welcoming thee
Will rouse my weary soul to live.
